main_text.p: Basilidem Hæresiarcham exhibet, à quo, inquit, Gnostici. Eusebio subjungit Theodoretum qui testatur lib. 1. Hæret. Fab. cap. 2. Saturnilum & Basilidem, ambos sub Hadriano fuisse; Et Isidorum Hispalensem qui Hadriani principatum exhibens, per idem tempus, inquit, Aquila Ponticus, interpres secundus post LXX. Oritur; Et Basilides hæresiarcha agnoscitur. Unum adjiciam testimonium ex Græca Historiarum Synagoge, quam cum Chronico Eusebia-no edi curavit Scaliger, depromptum; ibi enim auctor quisquis sit principatum Hadriani percurrens, postquam observavit Marcum primum ex gentibus Jerosolymi-tanum Episcopum constitutum esse, addit Tunc Saturninus Antiochenus & Basilides Alexandrinus, & Carpocrates variarum hæ-reseon patres & architecti agniti sunt; Marci autem Ordinationem refert Eusebius in Chronico ad annum Hadriani XIX. Domini vero CXXXVI. Duobus ante Hadriani mortem annis.

XXIII.Videamus jam quid Dallæanis argumentis repositurus sit Eruditissimus Vindiciarum Auctor; Observat primò pag. 82. Hieronymum in Catalogo, voce Agrippa, hæc habere. Mortuus est autem Basilides à quo Gnostici in Alexandria temporibus Hadriani. Putátque eum respexisse ad illa

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout. Ierosolymitanum and Jerosolymitanum: the initial I of the place name was changed to J as a consonant; Isidorum and Hieronymum keep I/H as printed. Word "hæ-reseon" at the line end: the second part is hard to read at the scan resolution and may be a misprint for a different form. The catchword "illa" is the final word of the page. Watermark "Digitized by Google" omitted.
